### Summary

The paper introduces a method called Higher-Order Multi-Instance Learning (HOMIL) for classifying whole-slide images (WSIs) in pathology. HOMIL improves classification by combining first-order (mean) and second-order (covariance) statistical moments of patch features within a WSI. It uses DBSCAN clustering to group similar patches, preserving diagnostic information while reducing computational load by processing common areas at lower resolution. Tested on the CAMELYON16 and TCGA-NSCLC datasets, HOMIL outperforms existing methods in accuracy and efficiency.

This lack of spatial awareness could limit the model's ability to capture complex patterns and interactions between different tissue regions.
